title: Reserved GPU selection and scaling playbook for enterprise intake
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a pragmatic playbook for triaging enterprise reserved capacity requests during intake. It focuses on mapping customer throughput objectives and business SLAs to a recommended reserved GPU profile and scaling policy (burst/reserved mix, autoscale thresholds, and pre-warm strategies). Goal is to standardize intake decisions so Solutions, Sales, and SRE can deliver predictable scoping and quoted SLAs within 2 business days for typical cases.

Background & motivation:
- Sales and Solutions are seeing variability in enterprise asks: some request simple throughput-only guarantees, others need tight p99 latency SLAs across mixed workloads, and some want bursty patterns with long-tail peaks.
- Current scoping is ad-hoc; infra and pricing teams report repeated rework when customers present atypical sequence-length or caching expectations.
- A repeatable playbook reduces time-to-offer and lowers risk of under-provisioning or overly conservative quotes.

Decision drivers (what this playbook balances):
- Customer SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, throughput (tokens/sec), request concurrency, and KV cache hit expectations.
- Workload shape: steady-state steady-stream, bursty with short peaks, or batch/periodic large jobs.
- Model footprint: sequence length, KV cache size, quantization level, and multi-GPU sharding needs.
- Cost & commitment: reserved vs burst commitment, commit length (monthly/annual), and pricing tier.

Core intake steps (operational checklist):
1) Intake form (Solutions) - required fields: target p95 latency at X token length, expected concurrent active users, peak qps, model family + expected sequence lengths, KV cache hit target, compliance region, desired SLA window (regional/24x7), and preferred commit term. Link to intake form: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated-intake-form
2) Fast capacity estimate (triage) - use throughput bands: Small (<=5k tokens/s), Medium (5k-50k tokens/s), Large (50k-250k tokens/s), XL (>250k tokens/s). Map bands to GPU classes: Small -> A10s/RTX-8k equivalent, Medium -> A100-40GB or H100-80GB soft, Large -> M60/H100 multi-GPU, XL -> multi-node pod.
3) SLA bucket mapping - Conservative (p99 < 2s), Standard (p99 < 4s), Economical (p99 < 10s). Each SLA bucket includes recommended reserved throughput and recommended burst buffer percentage.
4) Scaling policy template - three options: Fixed Reserved, Reserved + Burst (recommended default), Elastic Autoscale (for predictable daily cycles). Define autoscale thresholds and pre-warm rules.
5) Review with infra (SRE) - confirm kernel compatibility, KV cache sizing, and whether model requires sharding. Create infra advisory ticket if special config needed.
6) Quote & commitment proposal - include reserved baseline, burst capacity price, and recommended guardrails (rate-limit fallbacks, alternative model variants).

SLA / GPU guidance matrix (excerpt):
- Example: Request: p95 <= 2s, 20k tokens/s, 100 concurrent users, 2.5k average sequence length -> Recommendation: Medium band, 2 x A100-40GB with reserved baseline 25k tokens/s, burst 40% for 10 minutes. Autoscale policy: pre-warm at 80% sustained for 2 minutes.
- Edge case guidance: Very long sequences (>8k) or heavy KV usage -> prefer higher-memory GPUs or sharded multi-GPU. Note cost and added operational complexity.

Acceptance criteria for triage completion:
- Intake form fully populated and uploaded to the deal record.
- Baseline GPU profile and scaling policy recommended with rationale.
- Infra advisory ticket created if anything non-standard is required.
- Preliminary quote communicated to Sales within 2 business days.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Over-provisioning reduces margin; under-provisioning risks SLA breaches and escalations. Recommend conservative baseline + burst to mitigate.
- Complex models (sparsity, custom kernels) increase variance; these require deeper infra review and may push timelines.

Stakeholders & reviewers:
- Solutions Engineering (primary intake), Product (owner: Maya Rodriguez), Infra/SRE (review), Pricing, Legal (contract SLA language).

Next steps / Implementation plan:
- (Owner) Draft intake form additions and link field validations (Due: 2025-02-20).
- (Infra) Build a fast capacity estimator script and publish a Playbook page with examples (Due: 2025-02-28).
- (Pricing) Define burst pricing bands and commit discounts (Due: 2025-03-05).

Related artifacts and links:
- Draft playbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated-capacity-playbook-draft
- Estimator prototype (internal notebook): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/estimator-proto
- Example PR for autoscale config templates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1421

Notes on follow-ups and measurement:
- Track time from intake submission to quote and aim for median <= 2 business days.
- Monitor first-month SLA incidents for new deals and feed regressions into the Optimize roadmap.
